- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior high), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.80) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 1–3% to avoid overbought bias.
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment oscillating 0.27–0.77), model often fails to revert quickly; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of history.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the window when sentiment is positive; apply 1–2% downward correction for first 7 days if sentiment >0.7.
- If sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.80 to 0.00), model often fails to anticipate downward drift; add 1–3% downward bias for next 5–10 days.
